title: Weil extension by zero
statement:
Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an
open immersion of
separated finite-type schemes ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) over the
finite field $k_0$, with
base change $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ to the fixed algebraic closure $k$
of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a
strict Weil complex
$(K,\varphi)$ on $X$ in the finite-coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], set

$$
\bar K=j_!K,\qquad
\bar\varphi:
Lg_Y^*j_!K\xrightarrow{b_{g_Y}}
j_!Lg_X^*K\xrightarrow{j_!\varphi}j_!K.
$$

Here $j_!$ denotes the induced extension-by-zero functor on complexes
of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange], built from the module-sheaf functor
[def-weil-extension-by-zero], and $b_{g_Y}$ is the comparison
isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the Cartesian square
of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square].

split_report.summary: Audited the definition against the current trace-formula blueprint and the source library. The construction uses the six existing statement dependencies and requires no child nodes: the underlying complex is j_! K and its coefficient map is (j_! phi) composed with the open-square exchange b_{g_Y}. Made the finite-field base change and finite-coefficient conventions explicit and added the three missing inline dependency citations. No finished declaration with this exact statement was found in WeilConjectures. Second reading clarified that j_! denotes the induced functor on complexes supplied by the exchange statement.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the sole definition clause in def-trf-weil-extension-zero: bar K = j_! K and bar phi = (j_! phi) composed with b_{g_Y}.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q104-7ff3250af (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole definition, all six statement dependencies, the unit and the sources. The item text matches the master blueprint (order 2369) and main-20261015 (order 2713) hypothesis by hypothesis; those two snapshots have identical bodies. The delivery only adds inline citations for the three dependencies that were listed but not cited, plus one sentence saying that j_! is the functor on complexes. Nothing is weakened. The composite is well typed. lem-trf-frobenius-open-square at m=1 makes the square (g_X, g_Y, j, j) Cartesian. lem-trf-open-square-exchange accepts any g, including a semilinear one, at A=A_{E,n} on the small pro-etale sites, so b_{g_Y}: Lg_Y^*j_!K -> j_!Lg_X^*K. In def-trf-strict-weil-complex, g_gamma=g_X with gamma=sigma^{-1}, the same map as in the square node, so j_!phi starts exactly where b_{g_Y} ends. The coefficient category (A_{E,n} on the pro-etale site) and the base-change square (the m=1 Galois square) agree with the master source. Strictness of the new pair and functoriality are correctly left to separate statements, as rem-ptr-trf-weil-extension-zero-11 says. I checked Stacks 03S6 (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-shriek-base-change, line 11493): it gives the same exchange direction and is quoted only as the etale analogue. No SGA source is used. Edge cases checked: j=id gives back phi; an empty X or K=0 gives zero; a disjoint union gives phi(+)0; Spec k_0 works. Duplicate search: I grepped the whole DAG and went through about 80 definition nodes that mention extension by zero. def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange uses the same b map in a compact-support exchange, which is consistent and not a duplicate. There are no new nodes, no fixes and no tool_uses.
